cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: motivation – The reason or desire to act or move toward a specific goal.

p.em: Example: Finding inner motivation helps overcome past mistakes and momentum loss.

cosy-blockquote.p: direction – The course along which someone or something moves.

p.em: Example: Choosing to move in the right direction requires letting go of past regrets.

cosy-blockquote.p: tears – Drops of clear salty liquid secreted by glands in the eye, drawn by sorrow or relief.

p.em: Example: Wiping away her tears was the first step toward reclaiming her peace.

cosy-blockquote.p: fears – An unpleasant emotion caused by the belief that someone or something is dangerous.

p.em: Example: Facing your deepest fears allows you to step confidently into the future.

cosy-blockquote.p: reminiscing – Indulging in enjoyable or painful recollection of past events.

p.em: Example: Reminiscing about old mistakes can trap you if you do not focus on today.

cosy-blockquote.p: decision – A conclusion or resolution reached after consideration.

p.em: Example: Making a firm decision to move forward changes everything.

cosy-blockquote.p: progress – Forward or onward movement toward a destination or goal.

p.em: Example: Every small step forward counts as genuine progress.

cosy-blockquote.p: future – The time or a period of time following the moment of speaking or writing.

p.em: Example: The future belongs to those who learn from the past without being held back by it.

cosy-blockquote.p: courage – The ability to do something that frightens one; bravery.

p.em: Example: It takes courage to walk away from situations that no longer serve you.

cosy-blockquote.p: healing – The process of making or becoming sound or healthy again.

p.em: Example: Emotional healing begins when you forgive yourself for past errors.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: She is moving to the right direction → Correct: She is moving in the right direction ((Use the preposition 'in' with 'direction' when indicating general course or alignment.))
Incorrect: He stopped to reminisce of → Correct: He stopped reminiscing about his old mistakes ((Use 'reminisce about' or the gerund form after 'stopped' when halting an ongoing habit.))
Incorrect: It gave her motivation for continue → Correct: It gave her motivation to continue pushing forward ((Use 'to + infinitive' after the noun 'motivation'.))
